The invention relates to a power transmission device having two or more pistons for selectively transmitting rotational power. The device is configured to engage and disengage a power transmission path by applying hydraulic pressure to a piston module, thereby frictionally coupling a plurality of friction disks.

The power transmission device includes a housing assembly that defines an internal mounting space. The housing assembly may be formed by connecting a clutch housing, a clutch connecting portion, a clutch hub, and a disk housing. These components are joined together so as to provide a structural enclosure in which the operating elements of the device are mounted and supported.

A power transmission hub is disposed relative to the housing and is selectively and operably connected thereto. When the device is engaged, rotational power may be transmitted between the housing and the power transmission hub. When the device is disengaged, the power transmission hub may rotate independently of the housing, or the transmission of torque between the components may be interrupted.

A plurality of first friction disks and a plurality of second friction disks are arranged alternately within the mounting space. The first friction disks are splined to the disk housing so that they rotate together with the disk housing while being movable in an axial direction. The second friction disks are splined to the power transmission hub so that they rotate together with the power transmission hub while also being axially movable. This alternating arrangement allows the first and second friction disks to be selectively pressed together to transmit torque through frictional engagement.

The device further includes a piston module configured to apply an axial pressing force to the friction disks. The piston module includes two or more pistons that are actuated by hydraulic pressure supplied to corresponding piston chambers. When hydraulic pressure is introduced into the piston chambers, the pistons move and apply a compressive force to the alternating first and second friction disks. As a result, the friction disks are frictionally coupled, thereby enabling torque transmission between the housing and the power transmission hub.

Springs are provided to apply counteracting loads to the pistons. These springs may bias the pistons in a direction opposite to the hydraulic actuation direction, thereby assisting in disengagement of the friction disks when the hydraulic pressure is reduced or released. Accordingly, the hydraulic pressure and the spring loads cooperate to control engagement and disengagement of the power transmission device in a stable and reliable manner.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a clutch arrangement for selectively transmitting torque in a power transmission system. The clutch includes a friction disk assembly supported in or on a housing and configured to establish a frictional connection between relatively rotatable components when actuated. The friction disk assembly may include a plurality of alternating friction disks or plates, for example disks connected to a first rotary member and disks connected to a second rotary member. When the disks are pressed together in an axial direction, frictional engagement between the alternating disks enables torque to be transmitted between the associated members.

Actuation of the friction disk assembly is carried out by a piston module arranged to apply an axial force to the disk stack. The piston module includes two or more hydraulically pressurized pistons, each associated with a respective piston chamber. When hydraulic pressure is supplied to one or more of the piston chambers, the corresponding pistons are displaced axially and exert a compressive force on the friction disk assembly. By using multiple pistons and corresponding pressure chambers, the clutch can provide improved control over the engagement force, permit staged or variable actuation, and distribute the applied load more effectively across the clutch assembly.

The piston module may be mounted within or relative to the clutch housing so that hydraulic pressure can be supplied through suitable passages formed in the housing, a shaft, or another adjacent component. Depending on the operating mode, pressure may be applied to one piston chamber, to several piston chambers simultaneously, or to selected chambers in a controlled sequence. This allows the clutch to be engaged gradually, partially, or fully, depending on the torque demand and operating condition of the transmission.

To promote reliable disengagement and to prevent unintended drag between the friction disks, the clutch further includes return springs, separating springs, or a combination of both. These springs act in opposition to the hydraulic axial force generated by the pistons. When hydraulic pressure is reduced or released, the springs urge the piston or pistons away from the friction disk assembly and/or separate the alternating disks from one another. As a result, residual frictional contact is reduced, disengagement is improved, and the clutch can transition more predictably between engaged and released states.

The use of hydraulically actuated multiple pistons together with spring-biased return or separation elements provides a clutch arrangement capable of precise selective frictional coupling. The system improves control of clutch engagement, enhances disengagement behavior, and may reduce wear, heat generation, and parasitic losses caused by unwanted disk contact. Accordingly, the invention is particularly suitable for power transmission applications in which controlled torque transfer, compact packaging, and reliable hydraulic operation are desired.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest and most common words in the English language, yet it has an important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps identify a specific person, place, thing, or idea. For example, saying “a book” could mean any book, but saying “the book” points to a particular one.

Although “the” may seem simple, it gives sentences clarity and direction. It helps readers and listeners understand exactly what is being discussed. In phrases like “the sun,” “the ocean,” or “the future,” the word adds focus and meaning.

Because it appears so often, “the” can easily be overlooked. However, without it, English would sound unclear and incomplete. This small word proves that even the simplest parts of language can have great importance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical patent description for a multi-piston power transmission clutch including connected housing components, splined friction disks, piston chambers, and spring elements counteracting hydraulic axial force.
counterfactuals.output:
## Technical Patent Description  
### Multi-Piston Power Transmission Clutch

#### Field of the Invention  
The invention relates to a power transmission clutch for selectively transmitting torque between rotating drive components, and more particularly to a multi-piston hydraulically actuated clutch having connected housing components, splined friction disks, multiple piston chambers, and spring elements arranged to counteract hydraulic axial forces.

#### Background  
Hydraulically actuated friction clutches are commonly used in powertrains, transmissions, transfer cases, hybrid drive modules, industrial drives, and other torque-transfer assemblies. Such clutches typically include a clutch housing, a plurality of friction disks, and one or more hydraulic pistons that apply an axial compressive force to engage the friction disks and transmit torque.

In high-torque applications, a single piston may require a large effective pressure area or high hydraulic pressure to generate sufficient clamping force. This may increase package size, hydraulic demand, structural loading, and response time. Multi-piston clutch arrangements can provide improved force distribution and allow compact axial packaging. However, multiple hydraulic piston chambers can introduce undesired axial reaction forces on the clutch housing or adjacent transmission elements. If not properly balanced, these hydraulic axial forces can cause bearing loads, deformation, drag, uneven disk wear, or reduced efficiency.

Accordingly, there is a need for a compact multi-piston power transmission clutch in which hydraulic engagement forces are efficiently applied to a disk pack while spring elements provide a counteracting force or restoring force to reduce unintended axial loading and facilitate controlled disengagement.

---

## Summary of the Invention  
A multi-piston power transmission clutch is provided. The clutch includes a housing assembly having at least first and second connected housing components. The housing components may be fixed together by welding, fastening, press-fitting, splining, staking, riveting, or another torque-transmitting connection. The housing assembly supports or defines a plurality of annular piston chambers.

A clutch disk pack is arranged within the housing assembly and includes a plurality of friction disks. At least some of the friction disks are splined to a first rotating clutch component, and at least some separator or reaction disks are splined to a second rotating clutch component. The friction disks and separator disks are arranged in an alternating axial stack and are selectively compressed to transmit torque between the first and second clutch components.

A plurality of hydraulically actuated pistons is disposed in respective piston chambers. Each piston is axially movable in response to hydraulic pressure supplied to its associated chamber. The pistons may act directly or indirectly on the clutch disk pack to generate an axial clamping force.

Spring elements are provided to counteract hydraulic axial force generated within the piston chambers. The spring elements may bias the pistons toward a disengaged position, oppose an axial separating force between connected housing components, balance pressure-induced loads, or perform a combination of these functions. The spring elements may include wave springs, diaphragm springs, Belleville springs, coil springs, leaf springs, resilient rings, or elastomeric spring members.

The clutch thereby provides high torque capacity through multiple piston-generated clamping forces while reducing undesired axial loading and improving disengagement behavior.

---

## Brief Description of the Drawings  
The invention may be better understood with reference to the following exemplary drawings:

- **FIG. 1** is a schematic axial cross-sectional view of a multi-piston power transmission clutch according to one embodiment.  
- **FIG. 2** is an enlarged cross-sectional view of connected housing components defining piston chambers.  
- **FIG. 3** is a partial perspective view of splined friction disks and separator disks.  
- **FIG. 4** is a schematic view of spring elements arranged to counteract hydraulic axial force.  
- **FIG. 5** is a hydraulic circuit representation showing pressure supply to multiple piston chambers.

---

## Detailed Description of Exemplary Embodiments  

### General Structure  
A multi-piston power transmission clutch includes a clutch housing assembly defining a rotational axis. The housing assembly may be rotatable about the rotational axis and may be connected to a drive shaft, gear, drum, carrier, rotor, or other torque-transmitting member.

The housing assembly includes a first housing component and a second housing component connected to one another. In one embodiment, the first housing component forms an outer clutch drum, and the second housing component forms an annular piston support or pressure chamber body. In another embodiment, the first housing component defines a torque input member, while the second housing component defines a hydraulic reaction member.

The first and second housing components may be connected by a circumferential weld, an interference fit, axial fasteners, radial pins, a spline interface, a threaded connection, a crimped connection, or a combination thereof. The connection is preferably configured to transmit torque and withstand axial loads generated during hydraulic actuation.

### Splined Friction Disk Pack  
A clutch disk pack is disposed at least partially within the housing assembly. The disk pack includes a plurality of first disks and a plurality of second disks arranged alternately along the rotational axis.

The first disks may be friction disks having friction material bonded, sintered, sprayed, or otherwise applied to one or both axial faces. The first disks include internal spline teeth that engage external spline teeth of an inner hub. The inner hub may be connected to a driven shaft or output member.

The second disks may be separator plates or reaction plates having external spline teeth that engage internal spline grooves of the housing assembly or outer drum. The second disks are rotationally fixed to the housing assembly while being axially slidable relative thereto.

In an alternative arrangement, the friction disks may be externally splined to the housing assembly, and the separator disks may be internally splined to an inner hub. In either case, the splined connections permit axial movement of the disks while maintaining torque-transmitting engagement.

When the disk pack is compressed axially, frictional engagement between adjacent disks transmits torque between the housing assembly and the hub. When axial force is released, the disks separate sufficiently to reduce or interrupt torque transmission.

### Multi-Piston Actuation System  
The clutch includes a plurality of pistons arranged to apply axial force to the disk pack. In one embodiment, a first piston is disposed in a first annular piston chamber and a second piston is disposed in a second annular piston chamber. Additional pistons and chambers may be provided depending on torque capacity and packaging requirements.

Each piston chamber is at least partially defined by one or more surfaces of the connected housing components. For example, the first housing component may define a radially outer chamber wall, and the second housing component may define a radially inner chamber wall and an axial end wall. The piston may include sealing surfaces engaged by annular seals to define a pressure-tight variable-volume chamber.

Hydraulic pressure supplied to the piston chambers generates an axial force on the pistons. The pistons may act on a common pressure plate, on separate pressure plates, or on different axial regions of the disk pack. In one embodiment, the pistons are arranged in parallel such that their axial forces are additive. In another embodiment, the pistons are arranged on opposite axial sides of the disk pack to provide balanced application.

Hydraulic fluid may be supplied through one or more passages formed in a shaft, hub, housing component, cover plate, or valve body. The passages may communicate with the piston chambers via radial and axial ports. The chambers may be filled simultaneously or independently, allowing staged clutch engagement, proportional control, or pressure balancing.

### Connected Housing Components Defining Piston Chambers  
The first and second housing components may cooperate to define a compact annular hydraulic module. The first housing component may include a cylindrical wall having internal splines for receiving externally splined clutch disks. The second housing component may be connected to the first housing component at an axial end thereof and may include one or more annular grooves forming piston chamber cavities.

In one embodiment, the second housing component includes two axially spaced annular chamber recesses. A first piston is received in the first recess, and a second piston is received in the second recess. The pistons are sealed by inner and outer annular seals to permit axial movement under pressure.

The connection between the housing components may be positioned radially outward from the piston chambers to reduce leakage paths and increase rigidity. Alternatively, the connection may be positioned axially between the piston chambers and the disk pack to provide a direct structural load path.

### Spring Elements Counteracting Hydraulic Axial Force  
At least one spring element is arranged to counteract hydraulic axial force generated during pressurization of the piston chambers. The spring element may be disposed between a piston and a housing surface, between a pressure plate and a reaction plate, between connected housing components, or between the disk pack and a retaining member.

In one embodiment, a Belleville spring is positioned axially between a piston and the housing assembly. The Belleville spring biases the piston away from the disk pack when hydraulic pressure is reduced, thereby assisting clutch disengagement.

In another embodiment, a wave spring is positioned between the first and second connected housing components. When pressure in one or more piston chambers generates an axial separating force tending to move the housing components apart, the wave spring produces an opposing axial preload. This counteracting preload reduces axial displacement, limits housing deformation, and improves consistency of piston travel.

In another embodiment, a plurality of circumferentially spaced coil springs is disposed between a pressure plate and a reaction member. The springs oppose engagement movement caused by hydraulic piston force and return the pressure plate to a released position when hydraulic pressure decreases.

The spring elements may be selected such that their combined spring force is less than the maximum hydraulic engagement force, allowing the clutch to engage when desired, while being sufficient to reduce drag and restore the pistons to a disengaged position after pressure release.

### Hydraulic Force Balancing  
The multi-piston clutch may be configured so that hydraulic axial forces generated in respective piston chambers are at least partially balanced by reaction surfaces and spring elements. For example, pressure acting on a first piston may urge the first piston toward the disk pack while also applying an opposite reaction force to a housing wall. Pressure acting on a second piston chamber may generate a reaction force in an opposite axial direction. The resulting forces may be arranged to reduce net thrust on bearings supporting the clutch assembly.

Spring elements may further compensate for pressure fluctuations, centrifugal pressure effects, manufacturing tolerances, and disk pack wear. In certain embodiments, compensation chambers may be provided opposite the piston chambers and supplied with hydraulic fluid to reduce centrifugal apply forces.

### Operation  
During disengagement, hydraulic pressure in the piston chambers is reduced or exhausted. The spring elements bias the pistons and/or pressure plate away from the disk pack. The friction disks and separator disks are permitted to separate axially, reducing drag torque.

During engagement, hydraulic fluid is supplied to the piston chambers. Pressure in each chamber acts on the associated piston and produces an axial force. The forces generated by the multiple pistons are transmitted to the pressure plate or directly to the disk pack. When the hydraulic force exceeds the opposing spring force and frictional resistance, the disk pack is compressed, and torque is transmitted between the housing assembly and the hub.

During partial engagement, hydraulic pressure may be modulated to control slip across the disk pack. The multi-piston arrangement permits fine control of clamp force and may reduce the required pressure for a given torque capacity.

### Advantages  
The described clutch may provide one or more of the following advantages:

1. Increased torque capacity through multiple piston-generated axial forces.  
2. Compact axial and radial packaging due to annular piston chamber integration.  
3. Reduced bearing thrust loads by counteracting hydraulic axial forces.  
4. Improved disengagement response using spring return elements.  
5. Reduced clutch drag during release.  
6. Enhanced structural rigidity through connected housing components.  
7. Improved wear compensation and pressure control capability.  
8. Adaptability to transmissions, transfer cases, hybrid modules, industrial clutches, and power take-off devices.

---

## Exemplary Claim-Oriented Description  

A multi-piston power transmission clutch may comprise a housing assembly including a first housing component and a second housing component fixedly connected to the first housing component. A disk pack is arranged within the housing assembly and includes a plurality of friction disks splined to one of the housing assembly and a hub, and a plurality of separator disks splined to the other of the housing assembly and the hub. The friction disks and separator disks are axially movable and arranged for selective frictional engagement.

The clutch further includes a plurality of pistons disposed in corresponding hydraulic piston chambers defined at least in part by the housing assembly. Each piston is movable along an axial direction in response to hydraulic pressure supplied to the corresponding chamber. The pistons are configured to apply an axial compressive force to the disk pack.

At least one spring element is arranged to exert a spring force opposite to an axial force generated by hydraulic pressure in at least one piston chamber. The spring element may bias at least one piston toward a released position, preload the connected housing components against hydraulic separation, or bias a pressure plate away from the disk pack.

In certain embodiments, the spring element includes at least one Belleville spring, wave spring, coil spring, or diaphragm spring. The piston chambers may be arranged concentrically, axially spaced, radially spaced, or in a nested configuration. Hydraulic fluid may be supplied to the piston chambers through passages formed in the hub, shaft, or housing assembly.

The invention is not limited to the embodiments described above. Various modifications may be made without departing from the scope of the inventive concept, including changes in the number of pistons, spring configuration, disk spline orientation, housing connection method, and hydraulic supply arrangement.
